summary: Released condensed dMoE training drops task-loss gradients through routing weights. Exact softmax derivative witness proves a core backward mismatch even without pruning; historical result binding remains unresolved. Printed placement loop exceeds capacity, while all265 supplied maps are valid. Similarity superiority statement contradicted by fixed-budget tables; fixed-routing forward principle and packing bound survive.

problems.title: Released training drops task-loss derivatives of routing weights
problems.claim: Equation1/Section3.1/Figure6 and AppendixA describe equivalent weighted MoE computation with a backward pipeline; p8 trains all MoE modules.
problems.location: PDF pp3-6,8,13,15; router.py61-111; pre_dispatch.py48-59; dmoe.py224-243; glu.py195-197; condense.py111-125; kernels_mm_condense.py503-510
assumptions: Two experts/two devices with balanced one-expert capacity, top2of2, no pruning or jitter
Fixed nonzero input, realizable expert outputs1and3, logits(log3,0), weights(3/4,1/4)
Loss y^2/2, no topk boundary change; real-arithmetic counterexample
Current released trainable-router and condensed GLU path; no asserted historical run binding
problems.check: Weighted forward y=3/2; dy/dz_i=p_i(E_i-y), so task gradient(-9/16,+9/16). Source returnsNone for routing weights and uses no_grad across weight communication/condensation despite forward multiplying those weights.

problems.counterevidence: Forward inference can remain correct; expert and direct activation gradients are implemented. Auxiliary router loss can flow through separate path; no claim router never gets any gradient. Freezing router parameters alone does not generally restore input-dependent gate derivative.
